//: Dated acknowledgements for `scripts/audit-gate.mjs`. Read that file first.
An entry does NOT say the advisory is harmless. It says a human looked at
where the affected code is actually reached from, decided the fix could not
be taken on that day, and wrote down the date the decision has to be made
again. Past `until`, the gate FAILS on the entry - an acknowledgement that
cannot expire is a suppression, and this repository has already been bitten
twice by a rule that was only a fact somebody remembered.
Fields: `ghsa` (the GHSA id, as printed by the gate), `until` (YYYY-MM-DD,
compared in UTC), `why` (where it is reached from, and what taking the fix
would cost). All three are required; the gate refuses to run without them.
This is not the place to record an advisory with no published fix. Those are
reported and never gated, so they need no entry.

allow.why: js-yaml < 4.3.2, CPU exhaustion via empty YAML merge sources, in the PRODUCTION tree via electron-updater@6.8.9 -> js-yaml@4.3.1. It is genuinely reachable from a remote input: Provider.js:97 `parseUpdateInfo` runs `js_yaml.load` over the `latest.yml` fetched from the GitHub release, and AppUpdater.js:486 loads the shipped `app-update.yml`. The bound on it is that reaching it requires controlling the update feed - GitHub, or the maintainer's account - and anyone who controls the feed can already offer a whole installer, which electron-updater gates on the Authenticode publisher rather than on YAML. A hang is strictly less than that. Held rather than fixed because the fix is a lockfile bump to js-yaml >= 4.3.2 and three agents were editing this tree on 2026-09-10; `npm audit fix` on that day also wanted to add 40+ optional cross-platform binaries, which is not a diff to take blind. THE ACTION: `npm i -D js-yaml@^4.3.2` as an `overrides` entry, or a targeted `npm audit fix`, then delete this entry and confirm the gate goes green on its own.
